page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions) and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8).

Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). For fast local scratch operations, the instance bundles 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units (0.0 GPUs) and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results position the E32ds_v7 predominantly in the middle 50% across general compute and memory tasks, posting a PassMark CPU score of 48743.5, a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 34203.68, and uncached large block read memory bandwidth of 146.04 GB/sec. It demonstrates top-quartile performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.05 GB/sec and medium (7B) model LLM prompt processing at 190.8 tokens/sec. Text generation throughput on large (70B) LLM models drops to the bottom 25% (2.69 tokens/sec), indicating predictable boundaries for large CPU-bound neural network generation.

The presence of 256 GB of RAM alongside 1888 GB of NVMe SSD storage makes the E32ds_v7 cost-efficient for heavy stateful operations where external storage latency would degrade throughput. It is technically suitable for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise database operations, data analytics, and intermediate caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores) based on the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 256.0 GB of system RAM alongside an integrated 1888 GB local NVMe SSD. It features hardware extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and 480 MB of L3 cache, with no discrete GPUs attached. Benchmark metrics show competitive results across memory and compute tiers, notably achieving 53.04 million ops/sec in Redis SET operations and top 25% performance in single-threaded gzip compression (36.05 GB/sec). With balanced multi-core throughput and high local I/O density, the instance fits high-capacity memory-bound workloads including in-memory databases, data analytics, and caching systems.
